title: The Shell on the Flooded Path

passage.title: The Shell on the Flooded Path
passage.author: DRC BEACON Assessment Passage
passage.text:
Warm steam rose from the wet bike path in Piedmont Park after a loud summer storm. Maya stepped around puddles in her yellow rain boots and listened to water drip from the oak leaves. Strong gusts had blown pine cones and tangled twigs across the gray concrete. Near the stone bridge, the muddy creek was still rushing fast and high. Most neighbors stayed inside their dry homes until the clouds cleared completely. Maya liked walking right after the rain because the quiet park felt fresh and alive.

As she neared the willow tree, a round lump beside the wooden rail caught her eye. At first, she thought it was just a smooth river rock washed up by the flood. Then she saw bright orange spots painted across a dark brown dome. The small eastern box turtle, trapped between two heavy oak branches and a rising puddle, was carefully lifted by Maya onto dry grass. When her fingers touched its wet shell, the shy reptile pulled its head tight inside.

Maya knelt on the damp ground and stayed very still so she would not scare it further. She knew that wild turtles needed to stay near their own home turf to find food and shelter. Taking the animal to her house would only harm it. Instead, she looked for a safe spot on the higher hill where blackberry bushes grew thick. The soft soil under the bushes was warm and free from fast runoff.

Before moving the turtle again, Maya decided to inspect its shell for any cracks or scrapes. The heavy branches had only left a streak of brown mud across its back. While she waited in silence, the front hinge of the shell slowly opened a crack. Two dark eyes peeked out from the gap to check the sunny bank. After a long pause, four scaly legs pushed against the grass and carried the turtle toward the shade.

Maya watched until the orange spots vanished beneath the green leaves of the blackberry patch. She felt grateful that she had walked down the trail before bikes returned to the path. A speeding wheel could have struck the stranded animal near the bridge. Helping wildlife did not require a big rescue team or fancy tools. Sometimes a quiet walk and two gentle hands were enough to keep a small neighbor safe.

tier2Words.definition: left stuck in a place without a way to get out safely on one's own
tier2Words.rootHint: From Old English strand, meaning 'shore or beach where ships run aground'
tier2Words.contextClue: The turtle was trapped between two heavy oak branches and a rising puddle near the bike path.

tier2Words.definition: to look closely at something in order to check for damage or problems
tier2Words.rootHint: Latin root spect- ('to look') + prefix in- ('into')
tier2Words.contextClue: Maya looked closely at the turtle's shell to check for any cracks or scrapes.

tier2Words.rootHint: From Latin evanescere, meaning 'to fade away or disappear'
tier2Words.contextClue: Maya watched until the orange spots on the shell could no longer be seen beneath the green leaves.

tier2Words.definition: a cold-blooded animal with scaly skin, such as a turtle, lizard, or snake
tier2Words.rootHint: From Latin reptilis, meaning 'creeping or crawling'
tier2Words.contextClue: The box turtle had a hard shell and four scaly legs.

questions.prompt:
Read this sentence from Paragraph 2:

"The small eastern box turtle, trapped between two heavy oak branches and a rising puddle, was carefully lifted by Maya onto dry grass."

Based on the way this sentence is built, who or what performed the action of lifting?

options.text: The two heavy oak branches lifted Maya over the rising puddle.
options.childFeedback: The two heavy oak branches were lying on the ground trapping the turtle; fallen tree branches cannot lift a person!

options.text: Maya lifted the small eastern box turtle onto the dry grass.
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 2, the passive phrase 'was carefully lifted by Maya onto dry grass' tells us that Maya performed the action of lifting the small eastern box turtle.

options.text: The small eastern box turtle lifted the heavy oak branches by itself.
options.childFeedback: The small eastern box turtle was trapped between the heavy oak branches and was the one being lifted by Maya.

options.text: The rising puddle lifted the wooden rail onto the grassy hill.
options.childFeedback: A rising puddle of rainwater cannot lift a wooden fence rail onto a hill; Maya lifted the turtle.

questions.provingSentenceText: The small eastern box turtle, trapped between two heavy oak branches and a rising puddle, was carefully lifted by Maya onto dry grass.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 2, the passive phrase 'was carefully lifted by Maya onto dry grass' tells us that Maya performed the action of lifting the small eastern box turtle.
questions.parentExplanation: In this passive-voice sentence, 'The small eastern box turtle' receives the action, while the prepositional phrase 'by Maya' identifies Maya as the actor who lifted the turtle.
questions.retryHint: Look at the words right after 'lifted by' in the Paragraph 2 sentence to see who picked up the box turtle.

questions.prompt:
Read these sentences from Paragraph 4:

"Before moving the turtle again, Maya decided to inspect its shell for any cracks or scrapes. The heavy branches had only left a streak of brown mud across its back."

What does the word inspect mean as it is used in Paragraph 4?

options.text: To paint bright orange spots across a dark surface
options.childFeedback: The bright orange spots in Paragraph 2 were the natural markings on the turtle's shell; Maya was checking the shell for cracks, not painting it.

options.text: To wash away mud using fast creek water
options.childFeedback: Maya stayed away from the fast, muddy creek and simply looked over the shell on the dry grass to make sure it wasn't cracked.

options.text: To examine carefully for any signs of harm
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 4, 'inspect' means to examine carefully for any signs of harm, because Maya looked closely at the turtle's shell to check for cracks or scrapes before moving it.

options.text: To hide something deep beneath green bushes
options.childFeedback: After Maya finished inspecting the shell and waited quietly, the turtle walked under the blackberry bushes on its own.

questions.provingSentenceText: Before moving the turtle again, Maya decided to inspect its shell for any cracks or scrapes.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 4, 'inspect' means to examine carefully for any signs of harm, because Maya looked closely at the turtle's shell to check for cracks or scrapes before moving it.
questions.parentExplanation: The context clue 'for any cracks or scrapes' shows that 'inspect' means to examine closely for damage (Option C).
questions.retryHint: Look at the words right after 'inspect its shell' in Paragraph 4 ('for any cracks or scrapes') to see what Maya was doing.

questions.prompt: Based on Paragraph 3, why does Maya decide to leave the turtle in the park instead of taking it home?

options.text: She knows wild turtles need to stay in their own home area to find food and shelter.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 3 explains that Maya knew wild turtles must stay near their own home turf to find food and shelter, and taking it to her house would harm it.

options.text: She is afraid the turtle will bite her fingers if she carries it across the bridge.
options.childFeedback: The shy turtle pulled its head tight inside its shell when touched (Paragraph 2); the story never says Maya was afraid it would bite her.

options.text: Her parents never allow her to wear muddy rain boots inside the house.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 3 never mentions a house rule about muddy rain boots; Maya leaves the turtle in the park for the animal's own well-being.

options.text: The turtle is too heavy for one person to carry up the steep concrete path.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 2 calls it a 'small eastern box turtle' that Maya easily lifted with her hands, so it was not too heavy to carry.

questions.provingSentenceText: She knew that wild turtles needed to stay near their own home turf to find food and shelter.
questions.childTip: Paragraph 3 explains that Maya knew wild turtles must stay near their own home turf to find food and shelter, and taking it to her house would harm it.
questions.parentExplanation: Paragraph 3 explicitly states that Maya knew wild turtles must stay near their own home turf to find food and shelter, and taking it home would harm it.
questions.retryHint: Read the second and third sentences of Paragraph 3 to see what Maya knew about wild turtles and their 'home turf.'

questions.prompt: How does Paragraph 1 help set up the events of the story?

options.text: It explains why blackberry bushes grow best on sunny hills during the summer.
options.childFeedback: The blackberry bushes on the higher hill are not mentioned until Paragraph 3, when Maya looks for a safe spot for the turtle.

options.text: It shows that every neighbor in town came out to clean branches off the bridge.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 1 says the exact opposite: 'Most neighbors stayed inside their dry homes until the clouds cleared completely.'

options.text: It teaches readers how to tell an eastern box turtle apart from a painted river rock.
options.childFeedback: Maya doesn't spot the lump that looks like a river rock until Paragraph 2 near the willow tree.

options.text: It describes the storm damage in the park and explains why Maya is out walking on the path.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 1 sets the stage for the rescue by describing how the storm blew branches across the flooded park and explaining why Maya was out walking before anyone else.

questions.provingSentenceText: Strong gusts had blown pine cones and tangled twigs across the gray concrete.
questions.childTip: Paragraph 1 sets the stage for the rescue by describing how the storm blew branches across the flooded park and explaining why Maya was out walking before anyone else.
questions.parentExplanation: Paragraph 1 establishes the setting—a flooded, branch-strewn park right after a summer storm—and explains why Maya is walking along the path where she discovers the trapped turtle.
questions.retryHint: Check what Paragraph 1 tells us about the recent storm on the path and why Maya was walking while most neighbors stayed inside.

questions.prompt: Part A: Which sentence best states the central theme of the story?

options.text: Walking outside right after a thunderstorm is always safer than riding a bicycle.
options.childFeedback: The story is not about whether walking is safer than biking for people; Maya only notes that a bike wheel could have hit the stranded turtle on the path.

options.text: Paying attention and acting with gentle care allows ordinary people to protect nature.
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 5, Maya reflects that helping wildlife doesn't take fancy tools or a big rescue team—just noticing a creature in need during a quiet walk and lending two gentle hands.

options.text: River rocks and box turtles look exactly the same when they are covered in mud.
options.childFeedback: Mistaking the turtle's dome for a river rock at first glance in Paragraph 2 is just a small story detail, not the life lesson of the passage.

options.text: Wild animals can only survive storms if park workers build higher bridges.
options.childFeedback: The turtle was trapped between fallen oak branches and a puddle on the bike path, not harmed by the height of the stone bridge.

questions.provingSentenceText: Sometimes a quiet walk and two gentle hands were enough to keep a small neighbor safe.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 5, Maya reflects that helping wildlife doesn't take fancy tools or a big rescue team—just noticing a creature in need during a quiet walk and lending two gentle hands.
questions.parentExplanation: The central theme of the passage is that simple mindfulness and gentle action ('a quiet walk and two gentle hands') are enough for an everyday person to protect wild creatures in their natural habitat.
questions.retryHint: Read the last two sentences of Paragraph 5 to see what Maya concludes about what it takes to help wildlife.

options.text: "Sometimes a quiet walk and two gentle hands were enough to keep a small neighbor safe."
